notes:
ScreenTale 1.15.0 lets the camera fade in and out when a clip shows or hides it, lets a Spotlight sit beside its Arrow instead of underneath it, and makes the Timeline easier to work with.

- Showing or hiding the camera for a Camera clip now fades smoothly instead of cutting. Select the clip and use Show/hide fade in the Camera Inspector to choose how long the fade lasts, or set it to zero for a hard cut. Neighbouring clips that are both shown or both hidden no longer flicker at their boundary, and a fade keeps the outgoing layout on screen until it finishes.
- A Spotlight no longer has to sit underneath its Arrow. Drag the Spotlight in the preview to move only the bright area; the Arrow keeps pointing at the same spot. You can also use Horizontal shift and Vertical shift, Place beside arrowhead to put the bright area just past the Arrow head, or Centre on arrowhead to put it back.
- Command-scroll and trackpad pinch now zoom the Timeline around the pointer, like Option-scroll, and wheel zoom follows your Natural scrolling setting.
- A Zoom or annotation added while the Timeline is zoomed out is wide enough to see and grab, and is scrolled into view and highlighted.
- Camera clips show their layout on the Timeline, and hidden camera footage appears in grey with a camera-off icon. The Show/Hide camera toolbar button is gone; select a Camera clip and use Show camera in the Inspector instead.
